newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on exports and oversold signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on exports and oversold signals.

text.p: A bullish wheat number in USDA's weekly export sales report plus signals the market was oversold boosted CBOT wheat futures to a higher close, traders said.

U.S. net export sales of old and new crop wheat combined during the week ended May 8 totaled 705,500 tonnes, according to the USDA. That tally was above trade expectations for 350,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
But many traders said the main reason for the firm close was the fact the market was oversold after the recent slide in the July contract to one month lows.

Technical traders said the market was due for a bounce as the July nine day relative strength index early this week approached 30 percent. An RSI of 30 or less is viewed as an oversold market and an RSI of 70 or more is viewed as an overbought market.
Support also may have come from firm cash basis markets and the U.S. Great Plains weather outlooks were for only scattered showers in the dry areas of western Kansas.
Wheat closed unchanged to two cents per bushel higher, with May unchanged at $3.83 and July up 1-1/2 cents at $3.88-1/2.

LIT America bought two million bushels of July and sold 1.5 million July, traders said. Merrill Lynch Futures sold 3.5 million July and Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 1.5 million bushels of July with Smith Barney selling two million July, they said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, below the 23,823 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 800 July $4.20 puts at 34-1/2 to 35 cents and sold 800 September $4.00 puts at 24 to 25 cents, traders said. LFG Futures bought 400 September $3.90 puts at 19 cents and sold 400 July $3.90 puts at 14 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,500 contracts, below the 9,742 traded Wednesday.
